problem:
Calculate the product ${I}_{3}K$ given that ${I}_{3}$ is the $3\times 3$ identity matrix and
$K=[\begin{aligned}4 & 5 & 6 \\ 3 & 2 & 1 \\ -1 & 2 & -3\end{aligned}].$
worked_solution:
Any matrix, when multiplied by an identity matrix, remains unchanged (assuming that the multiplication is well defined).

The matrix ${I}_{3}$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix and $K$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix too. 

Therefore, the multiplication is well defined and 

$$
{I}_{3}\cdot K=K=[\begin{aligned}4 & 5 & 6 \\ 3 & 2 & 1 \\ -1 & 2 & -3\end{aligned}].
$$
